needs.text: Whether the tenant sublet, assigned, or otherwise parted with possession of the shop to Respondent No. 2 within Delhi DRC Act s.14(1)(b).

Whether Respondent No. 2's occupation was permissive employee/friend use with the tenant retaining physical and legal possession, or exclusive occupation/independent business indicating parting with possession.
How the burden of proof and rebuttal applies to claimed exclusive possession, business cards, billboard evidence, and the alleged absence of salary or commission records.
Whether claimed landlord knowledge or inaction, and any writing actually shown by the allowed record, bears on the statutory requirement of written consent or any protected sub-tenancy route.

How to preserve the procedural posture: Rent Controller and Tribunal dismissals, High Court allowance, and the present special-leave appeal without importing the withheld target Supreme Court merits or outcome.

objects.text: Santosh Kumar Jain / original owner / Respondent No. 1
Respondent No. 2 / alleged sub-tenant / claimed employee-friend
Shop No. 16 (Private No. 15), Gali Kunjas, Ward No. IV, Dariba Kalan, Delhi 110006

facts.text: The owner filed Eviction Petition No. 956 of 2007 before the Rent Controller under DRC Act s.14(1)(a) and (b) concerning the shop.
facts.speaker: NARRATOR
facts.quote: filed an application for increase of standard rent and eviction of tenant being Eviction Petition No. 956 of 2007 before the Rent Controller, Delhi under Section 14(1)(a) and (b) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958

facts.text: The owner alleged that the tenant illegally sublet, assigned, and otherwise parted with possession to Respondent No. 2, who was allegedly in unauthorized occupation and conducting an independent business.

unknown: whether any transfer or parting occurred
whether Respondent No. 2 had exclusive possession

facts.text: The Additional Rent Controller dismissed the eviction claim and directed the tenant to deposit the agreed rent for the preceding three years from filing.
facts.speaker: COURT
facts.quote: dismissed the claim of eviction while directing the appellant herein to deposit the rent as agreed for preceding 3 (three) years from the date of filing of the eviction petition

facts.text: The Rent Control Tribunal dismissed the owner's appeal from the Rent Controller order.
facts.speaker: COURT
facts.quote: The Rent Control Tribunal, vide judgment and order dated 24.03.2014 in RCT-203/2013/2011, dismissed the appeal.

facts.text: The Delhi High Court allowed the owner's petition challenging the Rent Controller and Tribunal orders.
facts.speaker: COURT
facts.quote: Learned single Judge of the High Court, vide judgment and order dated 07.11.2014, allowed the petition filed by the owner-Respondent No. 1 herein.

facts.text: The tenant appealed the High Court judgment by special leave to the target Supreme Court proceeding.
facts.speaker: NARRATOR
facts.quote: the appellant has preferred this appeal by way of special leave before this Court.

facts.text: The tenant claimed Respondent No. 2 was an employee managing the tenant's small business and was paid commission for services.
facts.speaker: TENANT
facts.quote: Respondent No. 2 herein was looking after the entire small business affairs of the appellant herein and is using and occupying the suit premises in the capacity of an employee.

facts.speaker: TENANT
facts.quote: The appellant herein is the lawful tenant and has never parted with the possession or sublet the suit property either to Respondent No. 2 or to any other person

facts.text: The tenant claimed Respondent No. 2 was only a friend whom he employed and allowed to sit in the shop, and denied that Respondent No. 2 operated M/s R.R. Jewellers there.
facts.speaker: TENANT
unknown: actual business identity at the shop
facts.quote: Respondent No. 2 is only a friend of the appellant herein and for this reason only he was employed and allowed to sit in the suit premises and no business was being carried out in the name of M/s R.R. Jewellers from the suit premises by Respondent No. 2

facts.text: The tenant argued that even assuming owner knowledge of a sub-tenancy in December 2001, the owner took no action then and had failed to prove Respondent No. 2's exclusive possession or the tenant's divestment of physical and legal possession.
facts.speaker: TENANT
unknown: whether owner actually had such knowledge
whether Respondent No. 2 had exclusive possession
whether tenant was divested of possession
facts.quote: even if the original owner was having knowledge of sub-tenancy of the suit premises in December, 2001, no action was initiated by him to vacate the same from the sub-tenant and hence he failed to prove that Respondent No. 2 is in exclusive possession of the suit premises and the appellant herein has divested himself from the physical and legal possession of the same.

facts.text: The owner claimed the tenant had sublet, assigned, and parted with possession of the shop in favor of Respondent No. 2, who was in illegal and unauthorized possession.
facts.speaker: LANDLORD
facts.quote: had sub-let, assigned and parted with the possession of the suit premises in favour of Respondent No. 2 herein, who is in illegal and unauthorized possession of the same.

facts.text: The owner claimed no document on record showed salary or commission payments to Respondent No. 2 and asserted that Respondent No. 2 admitted fixing an M/s R.R. Jewellers billboard in the shop.
facts.speaker: LANDLORD
unknown: scope and effect of the alleged admission
facts.quote: no document has been produced on record to show that Respondent No. 2 was being paid any salary or commission by the appellant.

facts.text: The owner claimed Respondent No. 2 printed visiting cards in his own name using the shop address and had admitted that fact; the owner also argued that once another person's presence is proved, the onus shifts to the tenant.
facts.speaker: LANDLORD
unknown: scope and effect of the alleged admission
whether the claimed burden shift standard applies on these facts
facts.quote: the sub-tenant of the appellant herein got printed visiting cards in his name with the address of the suit premises and the very same fact has been admitted in the statement given by him.

facts.text: The owner characterized the High Court as having held that the shop was sublet and that the tenant had parted with possession, and asked the target court not to interfere.

facts.stage: rival submissions about High Court judgment
facts.quote: High Court was right in allowing the eviction petition while setting aside 6 the judgments and orders passed by the Court of Additional Rent Controller and Rent Control Tribunal holding that the suit premises was sub-let and the appellant herein had parted with the possession
